question: Does the official EMB-hosted Navotas Coastal Bay Reclamation EIS provide accessible fishery evidence that can be reviewed without confusing key-informant catch reports with specimen-based occurrences?

sourceAccess.accessMethod: The official EMB EIS URL was opened through the web source reader on 2026-11-20, which returned the complete browser-extracted PDF text (15,269 lines). A normal unauthenticated shell HTTP HEAD request returned 403; no access-control workaround was used. No PDF binary or page image was retained or visually inspected.
reviewedSections: Cover: Environmental Impact Statement, Navotas Coastal Bay Reclamation Project, Barangay Tanza, Navotas City, 2020.

Section 2.2.5.1.2 and Table 2-33: fish visual census and dated coral/reef-fish spot-dive stations, including the report finding that associated reef fishes were absent across the impact area; separate evidence mode from fisheries interviews.

Section 2.2.5.1.4, printed page 2-158: fisheries primary data gathered through key-informant survey; interviewed fishers were asked about fishing activities, gears, catch composition, and fishing grounds.
Section 2.2.5.2.5 and Table 2-35, printed page 2-165: eight source-reported fish rows with binary impact-area and outside-impact-area columns.

The fisheries narrative attributes a separate group of vernacular/generic fish leads to Navotas CLUP (2011); the adjacent 2014 catch-rate paragraph concerns Pampanga municipalities and is not assigned to Navotas.

evidenceAssessment.projectAsReported: Navotas Coastal Bay Reclamation Project, Barangay Tanza, Navotas City, Metro Manila.
evidenceAssessment.reportedEvidenceMode: Primary data were gathered through a key-informant survey; several male fishers were interviewed about fishing activities, fishing gears, catch composition, and fishing grounds. Table 2-35 is reported in the same fisheries chapter, but its rows are not individually linked to respondents, dates, trips, or specimens.
evidenceAssessment.tableNameAsPrinted: Fish species and invertebrates caught in the impact and outside the impact area in Navotas shallow water

evidenceAssessment.relatedEcology: The EIS separately reports that associated reef fishes were absent across the impact-area spot-dive stations. That reef-fish visual-census result does not negate or replace the key-informant fishery table; the two sections have different evidence modes and scopes.
dateAndSampleLimits: No interview date, respondent count, fish-trip date, taxon-specific count, specimen voucher, or specimen-identification method is reported for the Table 2-35 rows.
Table 2-35 yes/no marks are category-level reports, not abundance counts or station-by-taxon records.
Table 2-33 dates the separate coral/reef-fish spot dives to April 4, 2016. Its stations are not linked to the fishery interview table; the date and coordinates must not be transferred to these rows.
The adjacent catch-rate paragraph names Pampanga municipalities and a 2014 fisheries survey; it is not a Navotas Table 2-35 sampling date or denominator.
A source-family discrepancy is preserved verbatim: the table prints Plotosidae for Arius manillensis. This family string is not taxonomically reconciled here.
localityLimits: The table describes impact and outside-impact catch areas in Navotas shallow water but gives no fish-specific coordinates, exact capture reach, or project/waterbody geometry.
The fisheries narrative says Navotas fishers may fish as far as Cavite and Pampanga; this broad context does not assign individual table taxa to those other regions.
This reclamation-project scope is not crosswalked to Tanza Marine Tree Park; shared Barangay Tanza wording does not establish feature identity.
sourceLineageLimits: The key-informant method is explicit, but the report does not establish that every Table 2-35 row came from an interview rather than another source in the EIS evidence chain.
The separate Leiognathus, Sillago, Gerres, and Salinas narrative leads are attributed to Navotas CLUP (2011) and are kept separate from the eight Table 2-35 rows.
No accepted-name crosswalk, voucher identity, current presence, abundance, catchability, diet, safety, or legal access conclusion is established.

rightsAndEvidenceDecision.decision: Retain the concise, source-attributed Table 2-35 labels and interview-context distinction in internal research only. The full PDF text is accessible through browser extraction, but no item-specific open license was identified and the page images were not inspected. Do not publish rows, photos, coordinates, or derived claims in the app until rights and taxonomic/locality checks are complete.

nextActions: Run a separate specialist taxonomy cross-check for the eight source table strings, preserving Mugil spp. as genus-level and the printed Arius manillensis/Plotosidae conflict until independently resolved.
Locate and assess the cited Navotas CLUP 2011 before treating the four secondary narrative leads as more than source-reported names.
Keep fishery interview claims separate from April 4, 2016 reef-fish visual census stations, Manila Bay regional fishing-ground context, and the Tanza Marine Tree Park study lead.
Review item-specific reuse terms before any public-app projection; NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.

sources.supports: The official EMB-hosted PDF full text, opened through browser text extraction, supports the EIS title/year, fisheries key-informant method, Table 2-35 source-reported fish labels and category marks, separate reef-fish assessment context, and printed page locators. No PDF binary or page image was retained.
Official EMB notice lists the 2020 project EIS, the City Government of Navotas as proponent, and Barangay Tanza, Navotas City, Metro Manila as project location.
